labels.label: the assembly: Causal.Causality.exists_c0_extension_skeleton (:221), _of_frontier (:194), _of_hasChronalNeighbourEverywhere (:232)
labels.notes: I compared each hypothesis with the target title. Title 'M connected, locally compact, Hausdorff' is [PreconnectedSpace M] [LocallyCompactSpace M] [T2Space M]; M is non-empty because W is. 'causally arc-connected' is hC. 'locally strongly causal' is hlsc, the named hypothesis Causal.Causality.LocallyStronglyCausal (DiamondConfinement.lean:378, node pending T-lad-c0-extension-nodes). 'W ⊊ M open' is W : Opens M with hproper. 'chronal neighbours at ∂W' is hchr, the declared edge hypothesis chronal_neighbour_at_boundary (ladder.toml:1099). 'W causally arc-connected and future one-connected' is hcac, hfoc. The one addition, hne : W non-empty, is necessary: for W = ∅ the conclusion's ∀ t ∈ [0,1), γ t ∈ W is false. It is implicit in Sbierski: the proof of Lemma 2.17 (:431) needs ∂ι(M) ≠ ∅, which fails for ι(M) = ∅, and so does footnote :406. It is disclosed (checklist :54, question 4). The conclusion matches the title term by term: D = C ∨ D = C.dual; a chronal curve of D over [0,1] with γ([0,1)) ⊆ W and γ 1 ∉ W, plus γ 1 ∈ frontier W (extra); D.FutureInextensible W (Ico 0 1) γ; and D.ExitDiamonds W γ. Taking N = univ in ExitDiamonds gives the title's Ũ, s₀ < 1 (also s₀ ≥ 0), the inclusion for s ∈ (s₀,1), and the compact closure inside Ũ. So the Lean statement is at least the target. The _of_frontier form asks strong causality only near ∂W, which is weaker. The _of_hasChronalNeighbourEverywhere form takes the node has_chronal_neighbour. Every hypothesis is a ladder property, a declared edge hypothesis, the named LocallyStronglyCausal/StronglyCausalOn, or a topological instance. No metric notion appears in any statement: Metric.mem_nhds_iff is used only inside a proof, on ℝ. Nothing is marked.

labels.label: the setting: Causal.Causality.ExitDiamonds (:115)
labels.notes: The 'stronger than the target' claim is true and correctly stated (#print of the definition). For every N ∈ 𝓝(γ 1) there are an open Ũ ∋ γ 1 with Ũ ⊆ N, an s₀ ∈ [0,1) and γ([s₀,1]) ⊆ Ũ such that: (a) for every r ∈ [s₀,1) and s ∈ (r,1], closure(I⁺(γ r,Ũ) ∩ I⁻(γ s,Ũ)) is compact and ⊆ Ũ; (b) for every r ∈ [s₀,1) and s ∈ (r,1), γ((r,s)) lies in the W-diamond, the W-diamond equals the W ⊓ Ũ-diamond, and it is contained in the Ũ-diamond. The target's conclusion is the special case N = univ, r = s₀, s < 1 of (a) and (b). (a) at s = 1 is Step 1.2's printed diamond (:528). The ⊆ of (b) is (1.2)'s ⊇ (:155–158). Conjunct (b)(i) makes the identified diamonds non-empty, so the setting is not vacuous. Every diamond is that of the causality D that the theorem chooses, so in the reversed case it is C's I⁻ ∩ I⁺. This is disclosed as question 2.

labels.label: the given-curve form: Causal.Causality.exitDiamonds_of_stronglyCausalOn (:131), exitDiamonds_of_curve (:182), IsSpacetimeExtension.exitDiamonds_of_curve (:405)
labels.notes: This is the hypothesis shape of Thms 4.10 and 4.11 (:785–793): a timelike γ of M_ext (or M_int) such that ι∘γ extends as a timelike curve to [−1,0]. In ETT that is a chronal curve of M̃ over [0,1] lying in W = ι(N) on [0,1), after the affine change of parameter disclosed in SCOPE. The forms ask only R₁ and local compactness, and strong causality at γ 1 only. They need neither γ 1 ∉ W nor v* → ∞. As REPORT finding 5 says, v* → ∞ implies γ̃(0) ∉ ι(M_ext) anyway: a limit inside ι(M_ext) would make v*∘γ converge. Lean ≥ the causal content. The metric divergence (Prop 4.14) and future one-connectedness (Prop 4.12, a hypothesis here) are layer 3, as disclosed.

labels.label: schwdef:extension via Causal.IsSpacetimeExtension (:281)
labels.notes: Def 2.15 (:403–411; :401 all manifolds connected; :228 Hausdorff, second countable, dim ≥ 2) read causally. IsOpenEmbedding is what a smooth isometric embedding between equidimensional manifolds gives (an immersion is a local diffeomorphism, hence open). range ι ≠ univ is 'into a proper subset'. ChartIso CN C along ι is Rem 2.3 (:249) for an isometric embedding that preserves the time orientation. '[Nonempty N], no connectedness' is accurate. Non-emptiness is implicit in Sbierski: Lemma 2.17's proof (:431) and footnote :406 both need ι(M) ≠ ∅. Dropping N's connectedness makes the notion more general, not narrower; M̃'s connectedness is asked separately as [PreconnectedSpace M]. One point is undisclosed (minor finding 1). The notion presupposes a causality C on M̃, i.e. M̃ globally time-oriented, with ι time-orientation preserving. Def 2.15 does not ask this, and Rem 2.16 (2) (:417) says explicitly that M̃ need not be time-orientable. That is the binder's reading R3 and the OPEN OQ-115. The closer's file and REPORT do not cite it, although SchwCausalLemmas.lean:81–84 does. The row is partial and unmarked, as it must be.

labels.label: the corollary for an extension: Causal.IsSpacetimeExtension.exists_c0_skeleton (:457), _of_hasChronalNeighbourEverywhere (:498), preimage_curve (:417)
labels.notes: It follows: the kernel checks it, with standard axioms. Its hypotheses are hι, hC, hlsc, hchr at frontier(range ι), CN causally arc-connected and CN future one-connected; they match the target's 'with the corollary for one'. Its conclusion gives the time-reversed pair (D, DN) with IsSpacetimeExtension DN D ι. It also gives γ chronal in M̃ leaving ι(N) at a frontier point, and γ = ι∘δ on [0,1) with δ chronal on every [0,s] and future-inextensible in N (Thm 3.1 Step 1, :485). Finally it gives ExitDiamonds on ι(N) and the identification of N's diamonds with ι(N)'s through ι. The transports ι(N) ← N (causallyArcConnectedOn, futureOneConnectedOn, dual) are needed, because the existing ChartIso.causallyArcConnectedOn (Causal/Remarks/MassiveManifold.lean:114, which reaches Causal.Model.Massive) and ChartIso.dual (Causal/MeasureTransfer.lean:95, which reaches Causal.SingularFlat) are model-layer by tools/ladder.py model_path. The new IsSpacetimeExtension.causallyArcConnectedOn is the converse direction of MassiveManifold's, not a duplicate. ChartIso.dual is re-proved inline in a single line. The stranding note is accurate.

labels.label: witnesses: timelikeLine_exists_c0_extension_skeleton (:527), exp_isSpacetimeExtension (:565), timelikeLine_exp_c0_skeleton (:575)
labels.notes: Neither witness is vacuous. W = (−∞,0) in the timelike line discharges every hypothesis of exists_c0_extension_skeleton by existing ETT-layer lemmas. exp : ℝ → ℝ is an open embedding with range (0,∞) ≠ univ. It is a ChartIso by timelikeLine_chartIso_of_strictMono, proved by the intermediate value theorem and injectivity. It satisfies every hypothesis of IsSpacetimeExtension.exists_c0_skeleton: ℝ is preconnected, locally compact and T2; the timelike line is causally arc-connected and locally strongly causal; the only frontier point, 0, has a chronal neighbour; and N = ℝ is causally arc-connected and future one-connected. So the hypotheses of both theorems are jointly satisfiable, and ExitDiamonds(b)(i) makes the identified diamonds non-empty.

paper_findings_verified.finding: (1) Thm 4.9, :798/:800: after 'otherwise reverse the time orientation of M_max', the next sentence uses '∂_u and ∂_v are future directed'
paper_findings_verified.verdict: correct observation; an IMPLICIT STEP, not an error of the argument
paper_findings_verified.notes: Verified. The orientation is fixed by ∂_u + ∂_v future (:706, :752). ∂_u and ∂_v are null and g(∂_u,∂_v) < 0 (:704, :750), so both are future null, and a future timelike X has X^u, X^v > 0. :800 is therefore true in the original orientation. After a reversal, ∂_u and ∂_v are past directed, so :800 does not hold literally for the reversed spacetime. The 'without loss of generality' is still valid, but only through a time-orientation-reversing isometry of M_max, and the paper does not state one. (u,v,ω) ↦ (−u,−v,ω) works: it preserves uv, hence H (:671, :748) and r, and du⊗dv + dv⊗du, and sends ∂_u + ∂_v to its negative. (u,v,ω) ↦ (−v,−u,ω) also works and preserves region I. The REPORT's own wording ('This step is not stated; it is harmless') is accurate. If this goes to the author it should be phrased as an unstated symmetry or imprecise wording, not as 'wrong'. The same implicit step occurs at :485 (Thm 3.1, Minkowski), where x₀ ↦ −x₀ is needed for Step 2.2's λ₀ → ∞ (:588–592); the REPORT does not mention it, and nothing depends on it.

paper_findings_verified.finding: (2) Kruskal model, :721: the maps (u,v,ω) ↦ (t_A, r, ω) are called time-orientation-preserving isometries for all four regions
paper_findings_verified.verdict: correct; a REAL SLIP (a false sentence), harmless where it is used
paper_findings_verified.notes: Verified region by region. Along a future timelike curve u and v increase. I = {u<0,v>0}: −v/u increases, so t_I increases, and ∂_t is future on M_ext (:654): preserving. IV = {u>0,v<0} (:676): −v/u = |v|/u decreases, so t_IV (:718) decreases: REVERSING. II = {u>0,v>0}: uv increases, so r = F̃⁻¹(−uv) (:698, F̃ increasing) decreases, and −∂_r is future on M_int (:664): preserving. III = {u<0,v<0} (:675): uv = |u||v| decreases, so r increases: REVERSING. So only I and II preserve the orientation, as the closer says. The only use is :809 ('since both regions are isometric'). The swap (u,v,ω) ↦ (v,u,ω) is a time-orientation-preserving isometry of M_max taking IV onto I: it preserves uv and the symmetric du⊗dv + dv⊗du and fixes ∂_u + ∂_v. With it the reduction holds. With :721's map for IV it would not: v* = t_IV + r* = 4m log|v| stays bounded or tends to −∞. The d > 3 sentence (:752) makes no orientation claim, as the closer says.

paper_findings_verified.finding: (3) §1 (:153–158): the 'i.e.' from future one-connectedness of the exterior to 'any future timelike curve in M_max from γ̃(s₀) to γ̃(s)' needs region I to be causally convex in M_max
paper_findings_verified.verdict: correct; an IMPLICIT STEP (true, unstated), in the sketch only
paper_findings_verified.notes: A future timelike curve between two points of I has u ≤ u_end < 0 and v ≥ v_start > 0 (u and v increase), so it stays in I = {u<0,v>0} (:673). The formal proofs (Thm 4.10 on M_ext, Thm 4.9's reduction at :809) do not need it.
